newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian denies killing American boy.
newsitem.headline: Italian denies killing American boy.

text.p: An Italian on trial for the murder of an American boy during a motorway hold-up said on Thursday that he had robbed trucks on the same stretch of road but denied he was the killer of seven-year-old Nicholas Green.
Michele Iannello, 28, who has turned state's evidence in other murder cases, said if he were guilty of killing the boy he would have admitted it because he had "nothing else to loose".
Iannello and co-defendant Francesco Mesiano are on trial in the southern Italian town of Catanzaro over Nicholas's shooting death in September 1994. Both deny involvement.

The boy was on holiday with his family, from Bodega Bay, California, when their hired car was chased and shot at in a hold-up attempt along an isolated stretch of motorway in the southern Calabria region.
He was hit in the head as he slept on the back seat next to his sister, then four.
The family's apparent lack of rancour and their decision to donate the boy's organs, saving the lives of six young Italians, earned the Greens deep respect and admiration in Italy.
Iannello testified that he had held up many truck drivers on the same motorway, but added: "I never robbed people in cars".
He also said he never used his own car when carrying out the robberies. Police found traces of gunpowder in his car because "my brother and then my cousin were killed in it," he said.

"Whoever shot at that car killing Nicholas Green could only have been crazy. You can't carry out a robbery, shooting repeatedly at a moving car. The chances of someone loosing his skin would be very high," Iannello said.

Iannello, who was arrested in November 1994, was released from jail last November 8 after turning state's evidence in the other murder cases. He is being held at an undisclosed safe house under a witness protection scheme for informers.
